count/row: An input of width W, here seven, and a filter of size F, here three. How many places can the filter sit?
count/slide: It starts at the left edge and steps one entry at a time, until its right end reaches the last entry.
count/count: That makes five positions, so five outputs: the width, minus the filter size, plus one, W minus F, plus one. The plus one counts the very first position.
pad/pad: Padding, P, adds a border of zeros on each side. With P equal to one, the input becomes nine wide.
pad/slide: Now the filter fits in seven places: seven, minus three, plus two for the padding, plus one. The output is seven wide, the same as the input.
pad/lose: That is no accident. A filter three wide loses two positions: seven in, five out. Padding adds two P, here two, which gives exactly those two back.
pad/five: A filter five wide loses four, so it needs two P equal to four: P equal to two.
pad/same: In general a filter loses F minus one positions, so with stride one, P equal to F minus one, over two, keeps the size. That is the usual choice.
stride/jump: The stride, S, is how far the filter jumps each time. With a stride of two it lands on every other position: four of them.
stride/formula: So divide by the stride before adding the one. W minus F plus two P, over S, plus one. Here, seven minus three plus two is six, over two is three, plus one: four.
stride/fit: The division does not always come out whole. Eight wide, with a filter of three and a stride of two: eight minus three is five, over two is two and a half, plus one is three and a half.
stride/drop: Half a position means the last jump would hang over the edge, where there is no input. So that position is dropped: libraries such as PyTorch round the size down, here to three. A setting fits exactly when the division is whole, and nothing is dropped.
try/p1: Try one: eight wide, a filter of three, stride two and padding one. How wide is the output?
try/a1: Eight minus three plus two is seven. Over two is three and a half, plus one: four and a half. A fifth position would hang over the edge, so round down: four.
try/p2: Now backwards: ten wide, a filter of five, stride one. What padding makes the output eight wide?
try/a2: With stride one the output is W minus F, plus two P, plus one. So ten minus five, plus two P, plus one, is eight: six plus two P is eight. Two P is two, and P is one.
